reports.title: Sanmina Reports Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2026 Financial Results

lines: At the midpoint of our full-year outlook, revenue is projected to grow about 27% and our non-GAAP diluted earnings per share about 24%.

desk.headline: Revenue up 84% to $3.86bn with ZT Systems, beat; first FY27 outlook points to about 27% growth
results: Quarterly sales jumped 84% to $3.86bn, well above the $3.48bn analysts expected, as the ZT Systems purchase added a large cloud and AI business.
Adjusted EPS more than doubled to $4.43 (GAAP $2.14); the adjusted operating margin rose to 9.0% from 6.0%.
For the full year, sales rose 79% to $14.53bn and adjusted EPS to $13.28 from $6.04.
Operating cash flow was $242m in the quarter, but heavier equipment spending cut free cash flow to $83m; $154m of shares were bought back.
Year-end cash was $1.68bn; total debt rose to about $2.09bn from $0.30bn a year earlier after the ZT purchase.

guidance.summary: Sanmina set its first fiscal 2027 range, implying about 27% sales growth and about 24% higher adjusted EPS at the midpoint, plus a Q1 outlook. The Q1 margin range is below the 9.0% just reported.

points: Q4 sales came in above the top of the company's own outlook; cloud and AI sales were $2.37bn, with ZT contributing $884m.
About $0.42 of Q4 EPS came from one-off tariff recoveries that management said will not recur.
AMD's Helios rack has started shipping in small volumes, a second AI platform is in the FY27 plan and a third is under discussion.
The wide FY27 range reflects new large programmes, component shortages and the timing of customer acceptance of AI racks.
Capex of about $450m is planned for FY27 (liquid cooling, testing, transformers); about $446m of buyback authority remains.

watch: How fast Helios and other AI rack programmes ramp, and whether margins hold in the 7.0–7.5% range as mix shifts.
Working capital and inventory build, and its effect on free cash flow and debt.
Component shortages that could push FY27 sales toward the low end of the range.
